tasks.short: Check and approve purchase and agency invoices in AFAS before the Rabobank payment batch goes out.

today.trigger: AP bookkeepers route invoices above the approval threshold in the AFAS workflow, and the twice-weekly payment batch is due.
steps: Open the invoice in the AFAS approval workflow and check it against the PO, contract or agency order
For staffing agency invoices, compare billed hours with agency portal hours and the site planning
Check for duplicates, changed IBANs and the budget line
Approve or send back with a comment
Release the payment batch to Rabobank
drudgery: Matching agency hours line by line across three portals
Chasing site managers by mail for missing approvals
today.time_sinks: Flex worker invoices in peak season (150 to 300 workers, three agencies) and chasing approvals for invoices without a PO.

lenses.faster: Rule checks on budget, contract, duplicate and IBAN change run before the invoice reaches the controller, so clean invoices arrive pre-checked and only flagged ones need reading.
lenses.autonomous: Each invoice booked in AFAS triggers the checks; agency invoices are matched to portal hours automatically and an exception list is ready before each payment run.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice line against hours and CAO rates, not a sample, and recover overbilling that today goes unnoticed.
lenses.joy: No more line-by-line hour matching; what remains is judging the real disputes with agencies and site managers.
lenses.options: For a disputed agency invoice, show three settlement options (pay, short-pay, hold) with the cash and relationship effect of each.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets the approval matrix, thresholds and check rules and reviews monthly how many invoices passed untouched and why others failed.
reach: Bookkeeper AP: first-line invoice matching
Credit and Collections Officer: supplier dispute follow-up
HR Administrator: flex worker hour checks against planning

tasks.human_edge: Authority over company funds and signing rights; judging a disputed agency invoice or an unusual payment request depends on context and accountability that stay with the controller.
tasks.pattern_why: Budget, contract, duplicate, IBAN-change and hours-match checks are written rules on structured AFAS and portal data with checkable outcomes; no model needed except for reading free-text agency invoices.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice booked in AFAS or agency hours file received.
steps: Pull invoice, PO, contract and agency hours via AFAS connectors and portal exports
Run duplicate, budget, IBAN-change and hours-vs-invoice rules
Auto-approve below the threshold when all checks pass
Send flagged and above-threshold invoices to the controller with the reason
Controller approves the Rabobank batch
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every invoice above the threshold, every IBAN change and the final payment batch.
data_needed: Supplier IBAN master data with change history
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history plus a check log on SharePoint kept for the auditor.

evidence.claim: Disbursement approval and cash monitoring fit deterministic checks with a person approving above a threshold.
evidence.source: Research digest, 'For the model' section (model knowledge)

evidence.claim: AFAS bank matching works on fixed rules for reference, IBAN and invoice number.
Cash allocation and similar decisions need mandatory human review with timestamped logs.

risks: Auto-approval below threshold invites invoice splitting
Agency portal exports change format and break matching
IBAN-change fraud if the check relies on supplier-supplied data
research_questions: What share of invoices last quarter would have passed all rule checks untouched?
Can all three agency portals export hours in a stable machine-readable format?
How much overbilling did a full check of one peak month of agency invoices find?

tasks.short: Watch daily cash, credit line and upcoming tax, pension and payroll payments so we never miss a deadline.

today.trigger: Every morning, plus before payroll, the loonaangifte and VAT due dates.
steps: Download Rabobank balances and statements
Update the cash sheet in Excel with expected receipts and payments
Check headroom on the credit facility and any covenant figures
Check upcoming payroll tax, VAT and pension fund payments are funded
Flag shortfalls to the Finance Director
drudgery: Copying balances into Excel every day
Rebuilding the expected-payments list by hand
today.time_sinks: Manual cash sheet updates and reconciling expected receipts with what customers actually paid.

lenses.faster: CAMT.053 statements and AFAS open items feed a daily cash position automatically; the controller reads it instead of building it.
lenses.autonomous: An alert fires when projected balance, covenant headroom or a tax or pension payment falls below a set level, with a short explanation of the cause.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling daily 13-week cash view per site, used by the business, not only by finance.
lenses.joy: No more morning copy-paste; the controller spends the time on the few movements that matter.
lenses.options: Show the cash effect of three scenarios, such as a large customer paying late or a peak-season flex ramp-up.
lenses.altitude: The controller defines the thresholds, compliance calendar and alert rules and reviews false alarms each month.
reach: FP&A Analyst: short-term cash forecasting
Credit and Collections Officer: prioritising which overdue customers to chase
Payroll Specialist: checking payroll funding

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to do about a shortfall, talking to the bank and judging covenant risk stays with the controller.
tasks.pattern_why: Bank data, open items and the tax calendar are structured; thresholds and alerts are rules. A model only writes the plain-language cause of an alert.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly CAMT.053 import and AFAS refresh.
steps: Import statements and open AP/AR from AFAS
Compute daily position, 13-week projection and covenant figures
Check the compliance calendar (loonheffing, VAT, pension)
Send an alert with explanation when a threshold is breached
Controller handles exceptions
in_practice.human_gate: Controller decides on every alert; no automatic fund movements.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI cash dashboard history and alert log in Teams.

evidence.claim: Cash monitoring fits deterministic checks with a person deciding.
Cash allocation needs mandatory human review and timestamped logs.

risks: Alert fatigue if thresholds are set too tight
Wrong expected-receipt dates make the projection look safer than it is
research_questions: Does Rabobank deliver CAMT.053 daily for all Noordhaven accounts?
How accurate were last year's expected-receipt dates against actual payment dates?
Which covenants exist and can they be computed from AFAS data?

tasks.short: Work out when we need extra funding or can park surplus cash, and advise the Finance Director.

today.trigger: Seasonal peaks, capex plans (forklifts, racking, trucks) or a cash surplus building up.
steps: Build a cash forecast in Excel from budget and AFAS actuals
Model funding needs for peaks and capex
Compare options: credit facility, lease, deposit
Write a recommendation for the Finance Director
drudgery: Rebuilding the forecast model each time
Collecting lease and bank offers into one comparison
today.time_sinks: Assembling data and comparing offers by hand.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the forecast update and an option comparison from AFAS actuals and offers; the controller checks and adjusts.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly funding-need note is drafted after the close without a request.
lenses.ambitious: Assess every capex request over a set amount against lease vs buy and cash timing, not only the large ones.
lenses.joy: Less spreadsheet rebuilding, more time on the actual choice and the bank conversation.
lenses.options: Three to five funding scenarios (facility draw, lease, phased purchase) with cost and covenant effect.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the forecast model and treasury policy; drafts come from the model.
reach: FP&A Analyst: scenario modelling
Finance Director: first draft of treasury policy updates

tasks.human_edge: The recommendation, bank relationship and risk appetite judgement stay with the controller and Finance Director.
tasks.pattern_why: Inputs are partly unstructured (offers, plans) and the result is advice; the person leads.

in_practice.trigger: Month close done, or a capex request or bank offer arrives.
steps: Pull actuals and budget from AFAS/Power BI
Model drafts scenarios and a comparison table
Controller reviews assumptions and adjusts
Controller writes and presents the recommendation
in_practice.human_gate: Controller signs off assumptions and recommendation; Finance Director decides.
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned forecast and recommendation memo on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Funding, planning and advice fit a copilot pattern; cash allocation stays human.
Estimates must be rebuildable by the auditor, not left in a personal AI account.

risks: Plausible but wrong assumptions in scenarios
Forecast kept in personal tools, not reproducible
research_questions: How far off were last year's peak-season funding estimates?
Would the Finance Director act on a scenario table instead of a single number?

tasks.short: Run the yearly budget and quarterly reforecast with FP&A and the three site managers.

today.trigger: Annual budget cycle in autumn and quarterly reforecasts.
steps: Send budget templates to site managers and department heads
Chase submissions by mail and Teams
Consolidate in Excel and check against targets
Hold review meetings and agree changes
Load the budget into AFAS
today.time_sinks: Chasing and consolidating submissions from three sites.

lenses.faster: Pre-filled templates from AFAS actuals and a model that checks submissions for gaps and odd jumps cut the consolidation work.
lenses.autonomous: Reminders and completeness checks run on a schedule; the controller sees only gaps.
lenses.ambitious: Driver-based budgets per site (volume, shifts, flex share) instead of last year plus a percentage.
lenses.joy: Fewer chasing mails, more time on discussing the drivers with site managers.
lenses.options: Present the board with three budget versions on different volume and wage assumptions (CAO increase).
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the budget process and driver model; FP&A and the model fill it.
reach: FP&A Analyst: consolidation
HR Business Partner: headcount and flex planning input

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating targets with site managers and directing the team stays human.
tasks.pattern_why: The work is directing people and judging trade-offs; AI drafts and checks.

steps: Generate pre-filled templates from AFAS
Collect and check submissions automatically
Model drafts variance notes and questions
Controller holds reviews and decides
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and Finance Director approve the final budget.
data_needed: Actuals by site and cost centre

evidence.claim: Planning and advice fit copilot at autonomy 2.

risks: Site managers trust a pre-filled number without thinking
Driver model too complex to maintain
research_questions: How many days does consolidation take today?
Which drivers explain most of each site's cost?

tasks.short: Advise the Finance Director and management team on results, risks and financial choices.

today.trigger: Monthly MT meeting, ad hoc questions, investment proposals.
steps: Pull figures from Power BI and AFAS
Analyse variances and trends
Write a memo or slides
Present and answer questions
today.time_sinks: Preparing slides and analysis for each question.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the monthly memo and slides from the close pack; the controller edits the message.
lenses.autonomous: A draft management note is ready the day the close is signed off.
lenses.ambitious: Answer every MT question within a day with numbers, including margin per customer and per site.
lenses.joy: Less slide building, more time on the conversation and the advice itself.
lenses.options: Several options per decision, such as price increase vs cost cut, with the effect on margin and cash.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets the reporting story and KPI definitions; the model drafts within them.
reach: FP&A Analyst: ad hoc analysis
Finance Director: first drafts of board notes

tasks.human_edge: Trust of management, reading the room and taking responsibility for the advice.
tasks.pattern_why: Advice is a human product; AI prepares material.

in_practice.trigger: Close signed off or MT question received.
steps: Model drafts memo and slides from the close pack
Controller checks figures and sharpens the message
Controller presents
in_practice.human_gate: Controller owns every statement in the memo.

evidence.claim: Accountants using AI closed the month 7.5 days faster; 62% worry about errors.
Advice to management fits copilot at autonomy 2.

risks: Drafted commentary states causes that are not true
Management stops reading if memos get longer
research_questions: Which MT questions recur each month?
Does the MT prefer a short memo or a dashboard walk-through?

tasks.short: Manage absence and WGA insurance, pension costs and benefits budgets, and track rule changes.

today.trigger: Policy renewals, pension fund and UWV notices, budget cycle, law changes.
steps: Collect premiums, absence figures and pension notices
Compare with budget and with AFAS absence data
Read rule changes (WIA, Wet verbetering poortwachter, pension law)
Update the benefits budget with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist
Discuss renewals with the insurer or broker
drudgery: Reading long insurer and pension fund documents
today.time_sinks: Reading notices and reconciling premiums to absence and headcount.

lenses.faster: A model summarises insurer, UWV and pension fund documents into a fixed template and flags cost changes.
lenses.autonomous: New notices in the mailbox trigger a summary and a budget-impact estimate.
lenses.ambitious: Link absence costs per site to insurance premiums and eigenrisico for WGA, so the business sees what absence costs.
lenses.joy: No more reading every circular; time goes to the renewal choice.
lenses.options: Compare eigenrisicodrager vs public insurance for WGA in three absence scenarios.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets the cost model and lets summaries and estimates flow into it.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: cost modelling
HR Business Partner: absence cost reporting per site

tasks.human_edge: Insurer negotiations and choices that affect employees, with the works council involved where needed.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured notices become structured summaries and figures inside a fixed budget workflow.

steps: Model summarises the document into a template
Extracts premium and rate changes
Budget model updates the estimate
Controller reviews and decides
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and Comp and Ben Specialist check every summary before it changes the budget.

evidence.claim: Insurance and benefit programmes fit llm_step summaries at autonomy 2.

risks: Absence data is health-related personal data under AVG; only aggregated data may be used
Misread policy clause leads to a wrong budget
research_questions: Is Noordhaven eigenrisicodrager for WGA or ZW?
Which absence data may finance see under AVG and the privacy policy?
Does the works council need to be involved in changes to benefits?

tasks.short: Check payroll results, loonheffing and pension deductions and book and reconcile them in the ledger.

today.trigger: Each payroll run (monthly staff, four-weekly shift staff) and the loonaangifte.
steps: Receive payroll journal from the Payroll Specialist in AFAS
Reconcile gross-to-net, loonheffing and pension totals to the GL
Check the loonaangifte and pension fund amounts
Investigate differences
Approve payment of wages and taxes
drudgery: Ticking totals between AFAS reports and the ledger
today.time_sinks: Finding the cause of small reconciliation differences.

lenses.faster: AFAS already computes the deductions; an automatic reconciliation of payroll to GL to aangifte leaves only the differences.
lenses.autonomous: Every payroll run triggers the tie-out and a difference report.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile every run per employee group and CAO, not only totals.
lenses.joy: No more ticking columns; only real differences.
lenses.options: Explain each difference with likely causes ranked.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the reconciliation rules and tolerances.
reach: Payroll Specialist: run checks
Accountant: payroll journals

tasks.human_edge: Approving wage and tax payments and signing off on differences.
tasks.pattern_why: Calculations and reconciliations are fixed rules on structured AFAS data.

steps: Pull payroll journal and GL
Run reconciliation rules
Report differences above tolerance
Controller approves payments
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves wage, loonheffing and pension payments.

evidence.claim: Payroll deductions fit llm_step drafts with a deterministic tie-out gate at autonomy 3.
Nothing should post until bank, AR and AP tie out.

risks: Duplicate work with the Payroll Specialist
research_questions: How many differences per run are real errors?
Can AFAS reports be pulled via API?

tasks.short: Prepare the monthly close pack, annual accounts and filings, and direct the accountants.

steps: Assign close tasks to accountants and bookkeepers
Prepare accruals, reclasses and depreciation
Reconcile balance sheet accounts
Write variance commentary
Prepare annual accounts for audit and KVK filing

lenses.faster: A model drafts accruals, reclasses and flux commentary; a tie-out gate checks before posting.
lenses.autonomous: Drafts are ready on day one of the close.
lenses.ambitious: Close in three days with a forecast the business trusts.
lenses.options: Several commentary versions for different audiences.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the close: accrual handbook, tie-out queries, materiality.
reach: Accountant: accruals and reconciliations
FP&A Analyst: forecast commentary

tasks.human_edge: Accounting judgement under Dutch GAAP and the auditor relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafting accruals and commentary from structured and semi-structured data inside a gated close workflow.

steps: Model drafts accruals and commentary
Tie-out checks bank, AR and AP
Controller reviews and approves postings
KVK filing via SBR tool
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every journal before posting.
in_practice.logs_to: Close checklist and journal evidence on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Claude Opus 5 scored 100% on four month-end scenarios where CPAs averaged 37%.
Leading model meets about 62% of criteria on 160 close tasks.
Trintech accruals agent drafts accruals for review and approval.
AFAS cannot file large company accounts via SBR.

risks: Benchmarks are US GAAP; Dutch GAAP untested
Audit adjustments if drafts are not rebuildable
research_questions: Which accruals recur and how stable are they?
Will the auditor accept model-drafted journals with logs?
How many days does the close take today?

role.altitude: From preparing the close and approving payments to designing the system: the controller owns the accrual handbook, approval matrix, tie-out rules, materiality thresholds and the audit trail, and checks how well the automated parts perform.
reach: Accountant: accruals, reconciliations and payroll journals
FP&A Analyst: scenario modelling and forecast commentary
Bookkeeper AP: first-line invoice checks
Credit and Collections Officer: prioritising collections from the cash view
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: benefits cost modelling
role.ceiling_note: Rule checks and drafts can save roughly 40 to 50% of hours on payments, cash monitoring, payroll reconciliation and the close; advice, budget negotiation, bank and auditor relations and signing authority stay human. Dutch GAAP and VAT are untested in benchmarks, so accounting judgement remains a limit.
skills_to_grow: Writing check rules and tie-out queries
Designing approval matrices and materiality thresholds
Reviewing AI drafts with audit evidence in mind
Data connections from AFAS and CAMT.053 into Power BI
AI governance under the EU AI Act and AVG
role.ambitious_version: A three-day close with a 13-week cash forecast the management team trusts, every agency invoice checked in full, and driver-based budgets per site.
